what_it_does: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a way of making AI language models smarter by first searching a database for relevant documents, then feeding those documents to the model along with the user's question — in effect giving the model a reference library to consult before answering. Different RAG setups (some search, some rerank results, some do multiple rounds of retrieval) have dramatically different performance characteristics: some are bottlenecked by the search step, others by the reranking, others by the actual text generation. Because of this diversity, treating all RAG systems the same way produces poor results. RAGO introduces a structured vocabulary ('RAGSchema') for describing any RAG pipeline in a uniform way, uses this to systematically measure and compare where each RAG variant spends its time, and then applies targeted scheduling and resource-allocation optimizations specific to each pipeline type — rather than applying one-size-fits-all fixes that only help some variants.
